On 13 May 2013 13:45, eyeguy <gpclar...@gmail.com> wrote:
I need to annotate a ggplot2 density graph, so I need the values generated for the y scales after the first layer is created:
Here is my code:
gg= qplot(ExpRef,geom='density',color=IOL,fill=IOL,alpha=0.8,data=tmp2,
            main=mtitle,xlab ="Expected Refraction",cex.axis=3.0,font.axis = 2)  #bold and cesx = multiplier);
    #gg = gg + geom_vline(data=data.frame(x=0,y=0),xintercept=lst$mus,color="black");
    ggp = gg + geom_vline(data=data.frame(x=0,y=0),xintercept=means, lwd= 2,color=I("red")) ;
    ggp = gg + geom_vline(data=data.frame(x=0,y=0),xintercept=PlanRef, lwd= 2,color=I("green")) ;
    ggp = ggp + annotate("text",x=PlanRef, y = 1,  label=paste('Planned Refraction'),angle=90,size=7.0,colour='black', hjust = 0, vjust = 0)
 
    ggp = ggp + annotate("text",x=SRKTRef, y = 0,label=paste('SRKT IOL-->'),angle=90,size=6.0,colour='yellow', hjust = 0, vjust = 0);
    ggp = ggp + annotate("text",x=SRKTRef, y = 1.5 ,label=paste('StdDev-->',sprintf("%5.4f",ThisGuyDF[1,'StdDev'])),angle=0,size=6.0,colour='blue', hjust = 0, vjust = 0);

In the last 2 lines I would like to place the annotated text at y max (not 0 or 1.5) but that depends on the scale generated in the qplot layer
How can I get my hands on the y (and/or x) scale values?
thanks
